hypotheses: H1: Second-line activity labels are driven mainly by lineage/tissue context, so choosing a line with a distinct tissue origin from A375 (e.g., HA1E, MCF7, PC3, YAPC) will more often yield one active and one inactive label than choosing another melanoma-like line.

H2: Second-line activity labels are driven mainly by compound-intrinsic target/MOA and assay/vehicle-threshold effects, so line choice matters less; any non-A375 line may produce similar active/inactive discordance, and target-matched lines (e.g., MCF7 for ER-related compounds) may not be privileged.
evidence_gaps: No measured second-line activity labels are provided; only availability and first_line are known.
Targets/MOA are database annotations (S3, S4), not causal or tissue-specific dependencies.
Activity is a vehicle-norm threshold in L1000, not viability (S5); two labels do not establish mechanism.
Transfer coverage and source choice effects (S1) and shared systematic response inflation (S2) are not quantified for these compounds/lines.
No information on whether A375 first-line label is active or inactive, which constrains expected discordance.
